newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Mining financier denies Zaire, PNG rebel links.
newsitem.headline: Mining financier denies Zaire, PNG rebel links.

text.p: Leading mining financier and developer Robert Friedland has denied press reports he was involved with rebel factions in Zaire and Papua-New Guinea.
In an interview with Reuters late on Tuesday, Friedland said he "had no involvement whatsoever" with either rebel group.
However he said he could understand people making the connection, at least in Zaire where the country's vast store of mineral deposits including copper and cobalt recently fell into rebel hands.
Friedland said his former co-chairman of Diamond Fields Resources Inc, Jean-Raymond Boulle, is in Africa and according to press reports had had contact with the Zaire rebel leadership.
But Friedland emphasised he had no interests in Zaire and no association whatsoever with Boulle.

After Friedland's comments, Boulle announced on Wednesday a $1 billion agreement between his new company America Mineral Fields and rebel leader Laurent Kabila's finance minister Mwana Nanga Mawampanga to buy a copper/cobalt project and build a 200,000 tonnes per year zinc plant.
Friedland also said reports in the Australian press that he had involvement with another group, Executive Outcome, were untrue. "I have no relation with this group whatsoever," he stated.
Nor was he involved in rebel activity in Papua-New Guinea. "I have never been there and have no involvement whatsoever," Friedland stated.
He was in Zurich on his way to talks with senior government officials in Moscow about oil and gas interests his holding company Ivanhoe Capital Corporation is looking to develop in Siberia.

Friedland, who was voted Canada's mining developer of the year in 1996, discovered the huge Voisey Bay, Labrador, nickel deposit which Diamond Fields subsequently sold to Canadian mining giant Inco. --Brian Spoors, Zurich Newsroom 411 631 7354
